chunks: Their prayer in the House was nothing but whistling and clapping, so taste the punishment for your disbelief.
ai.seo_question: What characterizes the prayer of the disbelievers in the Kaaba according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the contrast between the outward ritualism of the Quraysh at the Kaaba and their inner spiritual emptiness, where 'muka' (whistling) and 'tasdiya' (clapping) symbolize a lack of khushu (humility). It underscores the principle that true worship requires sincerity and presence of heart, not merely physical presence at the sacred site. This serves as a critique of performative piety, warning that ritual without conviction leads to divine retribution.
